statement: ELIMINATION WITH MERGING: RULE INCOMPLETENESS AND THE GAUSS CONTROL (Fable addendum A3/A6 tested; CLAIMED, Claude family). (1) Incompleteness: x=0, x=1, y=0, y=1 and the point (2,2) cover F3^2. prune+merge (scratchpad/aelim/merge.py) stops at 5 subspaces, where 1 suffices. The decision itself is correct (decide_m = covered). Rule set recorded as incomplete. The restriction-merge rule (resolution on a linear form) is not added, because a complete procedure decides 3-colourability (Fable Lemma G), so completeness is the decision problem itself. (2) Control (a), dense random linear systems over F3 with k equations in k variables, bad set = 2 hyperplanes per equation (Gauss-solvable): peak subspace count 28 at k=6, 278 at k=8; k=10 did not finish in 300 s. Brute force agrees. So the procedure blows up on instances that Gaussian elimination solves in polynomial time. Its subspace count measures this representation, not the difficulty of the instance. Consistent with Fable Lemma K (cube {0,1}^k, acn = 2^k, from a treewidth-2 instance). Controls (b) and (c) not run: (a) already settles the interpretation. Consequence for the contract (par. 6): counts from 17910/17911 and later G versus Prism(G) comparisons carry no hardness reading. Under fixed orders they compare only representations. The exact open step of this line (Fable A4) is a dag-like lower bound for resolution over linear equations mod 3. That is an open problem in proof complexity, would bound one algorithm family only, and is not an obligation of PNP-001. No obligation closed.

statement: EXPANSION POINT of the count identity (director's recollection; verify before citing): prod_e p_e(x) has an arithmetic circuit of size O(m) (one product of m small polynomials) - compact and cheap. The whole cost sits in ONE operation: the hypercube sum sum_{x in {0,1}^n}. A hypercube sum of a polynomial-size circuit is exactly Valiant's VNP form; VP vs VNP is open (algebraic analogue of P vs NP; cf. the Chukhin et al. 2026 PIT dichotomy already on file). So for the count identity the question 'where must the compact representation be expanded' has a precise answer - at the hypercube summation - and the open question is which variable-elimination orders keep the partial sums small for which formula structures.

Austrin-Risse and BGIP bound POLYNOMIAL CALCULUS degree (dynamic; PC degree <= NS degree). The two measures must not be equated: an NS upper bound of 3 implies PC degree <= 3, but a PC lower bound is the stronger statement. structure.question: Q-34b02a6004
structure.text: SOURCE CHECK row C (Stage A, lane T-B). Source: people.csail.mit.edu/rrw/MCSP-MKTP-stoc19.pdf (McKay-Murray-Williams STOC 2019), sha256 7077714ba22dead70fee16a58b46a7d556075a4037c1e2608e3a4fd92bcfc07a, read via web_read offsets 0, 4500, 9000. Theorem 1.3 (verbatim content): if some time-constructible s(n) >= n and A in PH are such that search-MCSP^A[s(n)] is not solvable by a poly(s(n))-space one-pass streaming algorithm with poly(s(n)) update time, then P != NP. Theorem 1.2: one-pass streaming for search-MCSP^A[s] in 2^n * s~O(1) time, s~O(s^2) update time, s~O(s) space, Sigma3SAT^A oracle queries of length s~O(s). Theorem 1.1: uniform AC circuits of size s~O(2^n s^2) with Sigma3SAT^A gates. Scope: the hypothesis is about the SEARCH version. A lower bound for the DECISION version of MCSP^A with the same s, A and poly update time implies it, since any search streaming algorithm yields a decision one. Update time is the operative resource; the paper notes that the algorithm may pause between stream reads. Row C is VERIFIED AT SOURCE. Review note: claimed steps S0005, S0007, S0012, S0014, S0020, S0040 are claude-haiku-5-5 (same family as the authors), so they need a reviewer from another model family. Not progress under the owner rule (bookkeeping).

statement: ADDRESSED TABLEAU W(t,i) + ALGEBRAIC EVALUATION UNDER P=NP (owner 2026-11-27; PI analysis; CLAIMED, Claude family; literature from memory). (1) Small circuits for W(t,i) of an EXP machine is the premise EXP subset P/poly (Meyer/Kannan route, PI reply 2026-11-27). Its algebraic version, the low-degree extension of the tableau, is Babai-Fortnow-Lund: EXP subset P/poly => EXP = MA. Under P=NP, MA subset Sigma2 = P, so P=NP => EXP not in P/poly. That is known, and it is no contradiction because the premise is not established (E subset SIZE(2^{o(n)}) contradicts the Impagliazzo-Wigderson hypothesis). (2) Which evaluations ev_S(U_G) does P=NP make polynomial? Boolean (SAT): yes. Tropical with poly-bit weights (min energy, an optimization in P^NP): yes. Approximate counting/marginals (Stockmeyer, in PH): yes. Exact N, Z (#P), F_2 (parity-P), F_p (Mod_pP), C: not known; Toda gives PH subset P^{#P}, the opposite direction. Hence the assumption P=NP does not unlock the exact algebraic evaluations of 17561/17584, so they cannot enter an 'assume P=NP, build a fast algorithm' contradiction as efficient subroutines. No obligation closed.

structure.relationship: S_fanout_001 addresses G0001(ii) by characterizing the exact internal fan-out sequence. The multiplicative composition formula from G0006 (c = log_d(r)) applied to the alternating fan-out [1, 2^n, 1, 2, ...] gives total leaf exponent c = 1 + (log_d 2) * floor((D-1)/2) / n. With MMW19's d = l/(100 s log s), this is c = 1 + O(log s / (n log l)) -> 1 as n grows. This confirms G0007/G0008's conclusion that the per-input-bit reuse exponent a (where r = O(s^a)) does NOT yield c < 1 under MMW19 parameters. The obstacle is not the fan-out magnitude but the fact that layer 2's fan-out of 2^n is exactly the input size, canceling the depth advantage.

structure.text: UNREVIEWED LEMMA (author family claude-haiku, same as this session; needs review by another model family before any use as a premise). STATEMENT: G a graph, c: V->{0,1} with sum_v c(v) even. T(G,c) is the CNF with, for each vertex v, one clause per local edge-assignment at v of parity != c(v); clause width = deg v. Let m = min{deg v : c(v)=1}. CLAIM: every resolution refutation of T(G,c) contains an initial clause of width >= m. PROOF: let x be the all-zero edge assignment. The clause at v forbids a local assignment of parity 0 when c(v)=1, so x falsifies it; x falsifies a clause only if c(v)=1, and then its width is deg v >= m. Suppose every initial clause of a refutation P has width < m. Then x satisfies every initial clause of P. Resolution preserves satisfaction by the fixed assignment x: if x satisfies C or y and D or not-y, then x satisfies C or D (if x(y)=1 it satisfies D, otherwise C). So x satisfies every clause of P, including the empty clause, a contradiction. SCOPE: GF(2) Tseitin CNF only; width only, no size bound. For G=K_n and c = indicator of one vertex, m = n-1. NOT claimed as new: this is a standard one-sided width argument for Tseitin formulas. CONSISTENCY: measured minima K3=2, K4=4, K5>=7 (cm-88c97aad7b8449b6, cm-235f5acd28484ce4) satisfy the bound. It says nothing about the GF(3) kernel encoding F(K_n) of Q-33e33ccf08, and it closes no named obligation (G0001, G0005 untouched). S0003 and S0004 remain CLAIMED.

statement: THERMODYNAMIC RESPONSE = AFFINE HULL (owner 2026-11-27; PI check; CLAIMED, Claude family). Z_G(beta,h) = sum_sigma exp(-beta H_G(sigma) + <h, X(sigma)>), X in {0,1}^{3n} one-hot. grad_h^2 log Z = Cov(X) under the Gibbs measure (exponential family). At h=0 and beta -> infinity the measure tends to the uniform one on proper 3-colourings (G 3-colourable; finite sum, continuity), so the limit Hessian is C_G = Cov_unif(X). statement: PB VIEW OF THE BLIND CASES (corrected): if every variable occurs in a clause, a NONNEGATIVE integer solution of A x = 1 is automatically 0/1 (x_i + x_j + x_k = 1 with x >= 0 integer forces each term <= 1). So positive 1-in-3-SAT is exactly 'does A x = 1 have a nonnegative integer solution' - the upper bounds x <= 1 are redundant and the information GF(3) misses splits into (i) integrality (30 of the 1,350 blind sets at n=6 have no integer solution; depth-1 CG from A x = 1 refutes exactly these, D-023) and (ii) SIGN (the other 1,320 have integer solutions, all with negative entries). The LP over x >= 0 is always feasible (x = 1/3, D-016h). Owner's worked example (clauses 012,013,023,045,124, n=6, GF(3)-blind): integer solutions exist, e.g. (1,0,0,0,1,-1) and (-1,1,1,1,-1,3) in [-3,3]^6, none nonnegative; refuted by clause differences, x_0 >= 0 and ONE rounding step (2t <= 1 => t <= 0) - a rank-1 cutting-plane proof using only nonnegativity.

statement: NORMALIZATION: SCOPE OF REVERSIBILITY AND THE THREE PROPERTIES (owner 2026-11-27; PI derivation; CLAIMED, Claude family). (1) Exact for the block constructions. The t-copy family (t copies per vertex, y_1 = ... = y_t, edges between all copy pairs; primal graph G[K_t], tw = t(tw(G)+1) - 1) preserves U_G by the monomial substitution X_{v,c} -> prod_i X_{v,i,c}. Hybrid elimination (17919) removes the linear block equations by substitution in polynomial time and returns G. The prism pipeline Prism(G) -> affine normal form -> block encoding -> coordinate change -> G is exact and polynomial (17921-17923). w_sem = tw(G)+1 throughout (17924). B(b,t) = t b and its mixed difference 1 are arithmetic of a bilinear formula with no complexity content. (2) Owner restriction: 'every semantics-preserving structural growth can be reversed efficiently' is NOT proved in general. It is proved only for these block constructions. (3) Three properties to keep apart: (a) semantic equivalence of two representations (same solution set or same U_G up to substitution); (b) existence of a normal form; (c) efficient computability of it. The prism construction has all three. (4) PI statement for general representations (folklore-level, no citation): let c map constraint representations to representations such that c(phi) = c(psi) iff phi and psi have the same solution set. A polynomial-time canonical form c exists iff P = NP. If c is polynomial-time, then phi is unsatisfiable iff c(phi) = c(false), so the coNP-complete problem UNSAT is in P. Conversely, under P = NP take c(phi) = the lexicographically first representation of size <= |phi| equivalent to phi. It is found by prefix search over a Sigma_2 predicate and is polynomial-time because PH = P. So efficient canonical normalization of general representations is another equivalent form of the hypothesis (family of 17920, Proposition E), and it relativizes. Existence (b) holds trivially by this definition; the content lies in (c) and in restricting the admissible operations. (5) Open question, precisely stated: for a fixed admissible class N (block-local bijections, linear substitution, existential elimination of locally determined variables), which structural invariants of a representation survive every composition of operations from N? Candidate: w_sem of the nonlinear residual. Its invariance under N is not proved. A positive answer measures what the mathematics represents, not decision complexity. No obligation closed.

structure.conclusion: reversibility exact for block constructions only; efficient canonical normal form for general representations iff P=NP

(1) #{t: t!=a_i} = 2 - rank[d; d^2], existence <=> d_i d_j (d_j-d_i)=0. (2) d_k=d_i+d_j: <=> d_i d_j=0 (carry). (3) in F_3[t]/(t^3-t): #common zeros = 3 - rank{f_j, t f_j, t^2 f_j}, pointwise in y. (4) t!=0,u,v: admissible (u,v) = Z(uv(v-u)) = union of lines u=0,v=0,u=v (7 points); excluded {(1,2),(2,1)} = line u+v=0 minus origin; contains no line, so conjunctions of affine exclusions are not closed under projection (invariant under affine bijections). statement: RETRACTION of one sentence of 17554 + owner theorem (2026-11-27; PI check fg_cov_check.py; CLAIMED, Claude family). RETRACTED: 'computing C_G is as hard as the hull' (only 'at least as hard' holds). THEOREM (owner): (A) G bipartite implies W_G = Q^n (colour one side 1, the other from {2,3}; each vertex of the second side is its own (2,3)-component, so b_K = +-e_v; swap the roles of the sides), hence dim aff = 2n. (B) For any H on n vertices, B_k(H) (each edge replaced by k = 2n+1 internally disjoint length-2 paths) is bipartite with P_{B_k(H)}(3) = sum_j rho_H(j) 2^{kj}, so P_H(3) = P_{B_k(H)}(3) mod 2^k. (C) Adding the edges of a bipartite graph one at a time: P_{G_i}(3) = P_{G_{i-1}}(3) (2/3 - sum_c C_{G_{i-1}}[(u_i,c),(v_i,c)]), using colour symmetry E X_{u,c} = 1/3. So exact C_G on bipartite graphs is #P-hard under Turing reductions, although the hull is explicit there. Checks: (B) mod 2^k and (C) product exact on random small graphs, 0 violations. Known-type (#3-colouring on bipartite graphs is #P-complete; from memory, verify). Counting hardness, not a decision lower bound.

structure.test: Can a succinct encoding of residuals for an MCSP-derived language preserve a comparable transition cost while keeping state width polynomial, including initialization and encoding construction?
structure.text: Explicit residual truth-table encoding gives a zero-gate coordinate projection for each next-bit update, but requires 2^(N−t) state bits at cut t. This isolates the tradeoff the QE* gap must address: representation-independent update lower bounds must account for state width and encoding/construction costs, since the residual transition alone can be trivial in a large encoding.

statement: OPENAI COMPRESSED-PAIR DIAGONAL, source audit (openai/math commit 3344da59991e, 2026-11-24; unreviewed manuscripts 'VP and VNP are different' (11-23) and family 379; PI reading of the Lean sources, Claude family). Model: Computes s p = table of s binary +,-,* gates, free variables and scalars, formal identity in MvPolynomial; VP/VNP standard (polynomially bounded arity and degree; VNP = Boolean-witness sum of a VP family). A grep over lean/OAI/Computability finds no sorry, axiom, native_decide or implemented_by. NOT CHECKED: no build and no #print axioms (toolchain v4.34.1 with its own Mathlib pin, 3137 files; local Lean is 4.35.0); internal compression/replay lemmas not read. CHAIN: separation_lower_bound (forall C>=1, q, exists N, forall n>=N, forall F with CharP q: n^C < circuitSize(P n)) <- uniform_of_pair_compilers <- uniform_of_native_compilers <- uniform_bound_of_local_programs <- Program.contradiction. OBJECT: P n = sum_{x in {0,1}^n} U_n(x) prod_i X_{i,x_i} (PairedFamily.lean), U_n(x) = acceptingCount x = number of accepting paths within n^{10^9} steps of the two-tape nondeterministic machine decoded from the self-delimiting prefix of x, run on x itself (UniversalMachine.lean). HOW CIRCULAR GROWTH IS AVOIDED: (1) the diagonal program D, the templates and the field solution are fixed before the length (quantifier order: C, q -> templates S,B and kappa -> program D -> threshold -> n); D has constant size and sits in the prefix of x. (2) The hypothetical circuit is never written into the input. A circuit of size <= n^C with circuit.polynomial = P n gives a label assignment of a graded parse grammar (Production n c: variables Fin n x Bool, width n^{c+5}, degree n) satisfying the integer system B_x - U_n(x) = 0, one row per x in {0,1}^n, plus fixed template rows (compressorEquations, 2^n + const rows, label count polynomial in n). (3) Algebraic descent (LabelEvaluator.Model): one prime p (equal to q, or with poly(n) bits in characteristic 0) and a finite slice of the zero locus with bounded point count and a normalized linear functional on its coordinate algebra. The value read back depends only on the equations, not on which circuit solved them. (4) D counts paths on its own input and obtains functional value + 1 mod p (LocalCertificate.false_of_processor), contradicting row x. Compression and replay make the counting fit the clock n^{10^9}; that part was not verified. FORMAL VS BOOLEAN: the equation rows, U_n, the machine D and the read-back are Boolean or counting semantics. Uses of the formal identity in proof order: (a) wire_expanders_of_small_circuits inside fixed_templates_of_small_circuits (geometric hinge: small circuits for P n give a wire expander or shortening; not analysed further); (b) exists_compressorSolution_of_circuit, which needs hpoly : circuit.polynomial = P n and produces graded parse labels up to degree n (CircuitGrammar.lean: arbitrary constants, no homogeneous intermediate gates required). FIRST NON-TRANSFERABLE OPERATION (proved obstruction for (b)): a Boolean analogue, 'every Boolean circuit of size s for f:{0,1}^n -> F_2 yields a degree-n graded grammar with poly(s) labels whose indicator evaluations equal f', would imply P/poly subset NC^2/poly. Proof sketch: a grammar with poly labels and degree n evaluates as a homogeneous arithmetic circuit of size poly(s) (the matrix-path identity of LabelEvaluator; this premise is not independently checked); VSBR/MRK depth reduction gives fan-in-2 depth O(log n log s + log^2 s); simulate F_2 gates by Boolean gates at indicator inputs. CHAIN: separation_lower_bound (forall C>=1, q, exists N, forall n>=N, forall F with CharP q: n^C < circuitSize(P n)) <- uniform_of_pair_compilers <- uniform_of_native_compilers <- uniform_bound_of_local_programs <- Program.contradiction. OBJECT: P n = sum_{x in {0,1}^n} U_n(x) prod_i X_{i,x_i} (PairedFamily.lean), U_n(x) = acceptingCount x = number of accepting paths within n^{10^9} steps of the two-tape nondeterministic machine decoded from the self-delimiting prefix of x, run on x itself (UniversalMachine.lean). HOW CIRCULAR GROWTH IS AVOIDED: (1) the diagonal program D, the templates and the field solution are fixed before the length (quantifier order: C, q -> templates S,B and kappa -> program D -> threshold -> n); D has constant size and sits in the prefix of x. (2) The hypothetical circuit is never written into the input. A circuit of size <= n^C with circuit.polynomial = P n gives a label assignment of a graded parse grammar (Production n c: variables Fin n x Bool, width n^{c+5}, degree n) satisfying the integer system B_x - U_n(x) = 0, one row per x in {0,1}^n, plus fixed template rows (compressorEquations, 2^n + const rows, label count polynomial in n). (3) Algebraic descent (LabelEvaluator.Model): one prime p (equal to q, or with poly(n) bits in characteristic 0) and a finite slice of the zero locus with bounded point count and a normalized linear functional on its coordinate algebra. The value read back depends only on the equations, not on which circuit solved them. (4) D counts paths on its own input and obtains functional value + 1 mod p (LocalCertificate.false_of_processor), contradicting row x. Compression and replay make the counting fit the clock n^{10^9}; that part was not verified. FORMAL VS BOOLEAN: the equation rows, U_n, the machine D and the read-back are Boolean or counting semantics. Uses of the formal identity in proof order: (a) wire_expanders_of_small_circuits inside fixed_templates_of_small_circuits (geometric hinge: small circuits for P n give a wire expander or shortening; not analysed further); (b) exists_compressorSolution_of_circuit, which needs hpoly : circuit.polynomial = P n and produces graded parse labels up to degree n (CircuitGrammar.lean: arbitrary constants, no homogeneous intermediate gates required). FIRST NON-TRANSFERABLE OPERATION (proved obstruction for (b)): a Boolean analogue, 'every Boolean circuit of size s for f:{0,1}^n -> F_2 yields a degree-n graded grammar with poly(s) labels whose indicator evaluations equal f', would imply P/poly subset NC^2/poly. Proof sketch: a grammar with poly labels and degree n evaluates as a homogeneous arithmetic circuit of size poly(s) (the matrix-path identity of LabelEvaluator; this premise is not independently checked); VSBR/MRK depth reduction gives fan-in-2 depth O(log n log s + log^2 s); simulate F_2 gates by Boolean gates at indicator inputs. P/poly subset NC^2/poly is open and believed false, so step (b) is the first operation that does not transfer without proving an open collapse. Step (a) is earlier in proof order but not analysed, so (b) is the first operation proven non-transferable. TRANSFERABLE PART (PI derivation): U_n(x) = #Sol(Phi_x) for a positive Exact-One formula. Take the tableau of the clocked machine, record the branch choice per step (rows have 0, 1 or 2 branches) and pad with deterministic idle steps after halting, so accepting paths correspond bijectively to tableaux. Use the Cook-Levin local cell constraints, made parsimonious and positive via T41 (constant 0 from E(T,a,b), E(T,b,c), E(T,c,a); long clauses split as in 17540). Input selectors: EO(y_{i,0}, y_{i,1}) with weight X_{i,b} on y_{i,b}. Then P n = generating polynomial of one Exact-One family Psi_n restricted to selector weights, with size O(T^2), T = n^{10^9}. Like Z_{G,q} (17540), P n is a projection of an Exact-One generating polynomial. Graph-colouring gadgets are not parsimonious (colour symmetries and gadget multiplicities); not established. STRENGTH: no Boolean lower bound follows; no obligation closed; the VP != VNP claim itself remains an unreviewed external claim that was not built here.

statement: RANK THRESHOLDS UNDER P = NP AND EXPORT REFRESH FOR FABLE (owner 2026-11-27; PI check). (1) Owner precision, checked. P = NP forces no polynomial rank bound, but it makes polynomially bounded rank thresholds efficiently checkable. rank(M) >= k iff some k x k submatrix is nonsingular. For an implicitly given matrix (exponentially many rows and columns, entries computable in polynomial time) and k <= poly, that is an NP predicate (guess indices, compute the determinant), so it is decidable under P = NP. For an explicitly given M, rank is in P unconditionally (Gaussian elimination), so the statement has content only for implicit matrices such as compatibility matrices indexed by colourings. Like 17920 it uses only 'NP predicate, hence decidable' and therefore relativizes. It yields no contradiction. Addendum B (Fable: padding lemma + compatibility rank) is to be recorded as negative knowledge per 17926; its text is still not in PI files. (2) Process measure: so that Fable reviews the accumulated knowledge, the research-graph export was rebuilt with the unchanged builder (scratchpad/exporttool/export/build_export.py). statement: Dispute K11-D5, revised. Source: MMW19 (STOC 2019, abstract verified via web_read of people.csail.mit.edu/rrw/MCSP-MKTP-stoc19.pdf): 'If search-MCSP[n^c] lacks Õ(N)-size, Õ(1)-depth circuits for a c >= 1, then NP not in P/poly.' Consequence: the earlier H2 (a size transfer from NP in P/poly to small MCSP circuits) is not a separate premise; the cited theorem performs that transfer. Bare-chain objection applies only to a lower bound without the stated size/depth class. H1 (for every fixed k, CC(MCSP[m^c]) > N(log N)^k infinitely often, general circuits) lacks Õ(N)-size circuits of any depth, so it implies the MMW hypothesis for c fixed. OPEN: (a) the exact theorem text (hypotheses and 'lacks' = for all or infinitely many input lengths); (b) the decision-to-search step: H1 for decision CC implies search lack, since a search-MCSP circuit for size m^c can be checked against the table in N·polylog time; (c) the quantifier. Not a P != NP claim. The arithmetic table cm-908028e6543b4a10 is exploratory and does not bear on H2.

statement: ALGORITHM-STRUCTURE DIRECTION MAPPED TO EXISTING RESULTS (owner proposal 2026-11-27: apply the universal function to a hypothetical polynomial-time solver instead of the solution set; PI graph check before derivation). (1) Already in the graph. T43 Lemma B (2026-11-18): every fan-in-2 circuit C of size s has a parsimonious positive 1-in-3 encoding phi_C (read <= 3, O(s) variables, input set X, exactly one extension per accepting input), built in time poly(s). This is the owner's 'algorithm graph H_n'. T43 sec. 4: the uniform bridge P != NP would need is a P-uniform, scaled-down algorithmic method (nontrivial SAT algorithm against P-uniform circuits plus diagonalization inside NP); not known. 17143: exclusion criterion 'black-box bound with no white-box transfer'. 17359: P != NP is uniform, natural proofs concern circuit lower bounds, relativization and algebrization concern every uniform route. (2) What the construction forces (PI). Under P = NP, a P-uniform circuit family C_n computes the selection S (Fable Prop E). H_n = phi_{C_n} gives U_{H_n}(X,Y) = sum over inputs x of X^x Y^{comp(x)}: one monomial per input. The only relation forced between U_G and U_{H_n} is correctness: the output part of the monomial for input G is a monomial of U_G, or the UNSAT symbol iff U_G = 0. The internal gates are unconstrained beyond correctness and uniformity. Any further forced property of the gates is a P-uniform circuit lower bound for S, which is equivalent to P != NP (T45 Lemma T5). (3) Barrier placement. White-box use of the gates avoids relativization only if a step uses the gate structure. An algebraic analysis of U_{H_n} (arithmetization of the computation) is the setting of Aaronson-Wigderson algebrization (cited from memory, verify at source): such steps algebrize unless they use more than low-degree extensions. A property derived from truth tables of the circuits must avoid the natural-proofs conditions (largeness, constructivity). (4) Unused joint consequence (candidate, owner to decide): T43 Q-BD asks whether satisfiability of Lemma-B images phi_C with functional backdoor X (|X| = n) is decidable in 2^n / n^{omega(1)} poly(|phi|). The hybrid elimination of 17919/17921 is exactly a tool for that structure: clauses are linear equations mod 3, the rest is forced by the backdoor. A saving gives NEXP not in P/poly via Williams (not P != NP; T43). This is a concrete point where the new mathematics meets an existing bridge without a lower-bound premise. No obligation closed.

statement: BIT-COST RULE for every algorithmic claim in PNP-001 (owner 2026-11-19, physical vs abstract model): costs are counted in bits on the classical model. Operations on numbers whose size grows with n (exact counts Z(F) = sum_x prod_e p_e(x), polynomial coefficients, determinants, rational solutions, tensor entries) are charged by their bit length; a method that is polynomial only under unit-cost arithmetic is not a polynomial algorithm (unit-cost multiplication RAM = PSPACE). A faster physical or alternative model counts for P = NP only if it is classically simulable with polynomial overhead.

Use mu(F,pi) = max_t log2 K_t(F,pi) only for intermediate results of a FIXED construction plan (H-CONSTRUCT-002), bounding that plan class only. Proven transfers exist for restricted models (OBDD solvers incl. dynamic order, Itsykson-Ovcharov SAT 2024; DNNF via rectangle covers; one-tape TM palindromes Omega(n^2)). S0015 (stage unrolling): the argument is sound for an oracle-free RAM with per-interval worst-case gap tau: padding to exactly tau steps is x-independent, and each step is poly(S*w) gates. GAP: MMW Thm 1.2 uses Sigma3SAT^A oracle calls of length O~(t), so a step is not a Boolean circuit of size poly(S*w). The stage must be restated as an A-oracle circuit with Sigma3SAT^A gates, with the oracle-gate count per interval and gate length counted. The lemma also assumes input bits are read in order. S0016(a): correct under the same caveat; the padding length u does not depend on x. S0016(b): t_i(x) <= sum_j t_j(x) <= N*u is correct, giving N^2*u*poly(S*w); the bound is weak but valid. Source support: the MMW Sec. 4 text states worst-case update O~(t^2) (see S-bb3fb4e44c), which supports the per-interval reading for the oracle version. Open: the oracle-gate restatement (new obligation), and an independent-family review. No computation supports this note.

structure.conclusion: CERTIFICATES vs P=NP (sources READ by subagents: Grochow-Pitassi arXiv 1404.3820 Def 1.1, Prop 1.4, Prop 2.2, Thm 3.1, Lemma 3.2, Lemma 1.12; Li-Pires-Robere ITCS24 Thm 20/44; Goos et al ECCC TR22-058 abstract; Pudlak-Sgall NOT opened). (a) Established: no source says P=NP gives poly-size IPS/PC refutations; P=NP gives only SOME p-bounded proof system (NP=coNP, Cook-Reckhow). GP Prop 1.4: poly IPS for all tautologies => NP in coMA and PH collapse to level 2 (necessary, consistent with P=NP). GP Lemma 3.2 + Thm 3.1: every CNF tautology has Hilbert-like certificates in VNP0, so VP=VNP => poly-size Hilbert-like IPS for all CNF tautologies; Pitassi: Hilbert-like IPS p-simulates Frege (EF with essentially same proof). (b) Own derivation (simple): IPS verification is PIT in coRP; under P=NP, BPP=P (Sipser-Gacs-Lautemann, Sigma2=P), so IPS becomes a deterministically checkable Cook-Reckhow proof system; p-boundedness still not implied. (c) Link to T50: MT <=> VP=VNP (our T50) => poly IPS for every tautology => coNP in MA; so MT is a strictly stronger hypothesis than P=NP and a candidate for a CONTRADICTION-free consequence check, not a consequence of P=NP. (d) RECALLED, NOT VERIFIED: Beigel-Buhrman-Fortnow 1998 oracle with P=NP and P != parity-P; if true, P=NP does not relativizingly give VNP_F2 = VP, so any use of VNP-power (Hrubes Thm 7, Q_S) from P=NP alone needs a non-relativizing step. Open: does P=NP (with canonical selector W) imply VP=VNP over F2 or F3 by a non-relativizing argument? Unanswered. Interface Boolean ring identity (18306) is not a new theorem.

statement: REFINEMENT of 17548: first formal step pinned (PI source reading, commit 3344da5). In proof order, the hypothesis first enters through fixed_templates_of_small_circuits -> wire_expanders_of_small_circuits -> cube_obstruction (l >= 18C^2: small circuits for P n exclude the Euclidean cube from every spectral wire metric) -> not_small_universal_of_exact_tensorPower_layout / sharp_tensor_layout (every tensor's powers are projections of P_M: TensorPowerCNF.sharp_projection) -> BalancedPowerObstruction -> Circuit.spectralValue_le_balanced_cost -> Circuit.exists_balanced_cutFactors. That lemma is the first formal operation: from c.exists_parseGrammar and homogeneousComponent, every party-selecting coefficient equals sum_S M_S over balanced cuts (|I| <= 3|S| <= 2|I|) with rank M_S <= |I|(|I||J| + s + 1). It uses the degree grading of a formal circuit. Everything after it (spectral values, layouts, cube geometry) uses only these cut factors. BOOLEAN ANALOGUE fails at exactly this lemma: (owner theorem, PI check) the AC0 predicate 'A is a permutation matrix with a_{11} = 1, B has exactly one 1 per row, and not a_{k,i} or not a_{k+1,j} or b_{ij} cyclically' has exactly one accepted (A, B) per directed Hamiltonian cycle. Its generating polynomial projects (X = 1, Y_{ij,0} = 1, Y_{ij,1} = z_{ij}) onto HC_N. Classically (Valiant 1979, from memory) the permutation-matrix predicate alone gives the permanent. Hence 'small Boolean predicate => small formal generating polynomial' for AC0 would put HC and perm in VP, i.e. VP = VNP. This is unconditional and does not use OpenAI; with OpenAI's claimed bound it would be false. The analogue of exists_balanced_cutFactors for Boolean circuits is therefore not a lemma that can be proved without settling VP vs VNP. STRENGTH: locates the non-transferable step; no Boolean lower bound; no obligation closed.

statement: CORRECTION (owner review 2026-11-20) of the evaluation of the biology-motivated directions: FB1 and FB2 decide only their own models (unconstrained stability; number of distinguishable states). They do not decide costs under robustness, bounded precision or local dynamics, nor the cost of changing representation. The statement "no route" was too strong. Completeness dilemma for a representation-change cost W_T: if T contains all polynomial-time transformations, a superpolynomial W_T for an NP family is P != NP itself; if T is restricted, W_T lower bounds are lower bounds for an algorithm class - useful for P != NP only through a theorem that T simulates every polynomial-time algorithm at bounded cost.

statement: POTTS DEGREE-2 DECOMPOSITION (owner 2026-11-27 local sums; PI global identity, potts_check.py: 200 random graphs, exact polynomial equality; CLAIMED, Claude family). H_G(sigma) = #monochromatic edges, Z_G(x) = sum over 3-colourings of x^{H_G}, x = e^{-1/T}; rho_G(k) are its coefficients; F(G) in SAT iff rho_G(0) > 0. For p of degree 2 with neighbours u, v: local sums 2 + x^2 (sigma(u) = sigma(v)) and 1 + 2x (otherwise). Hence Z_G(x) = (1+2x) Z_{G-p}(x) + (1-x)^2 Z_{(G-p)/uv}(x), with contraction as a multigraph (parallel edges kept, a loop from uv in E contributes x). At x=0: P_G(3) = P_{G-p}(3) + P_{(G-p)/uv}(3), and e_p in W_G (17507) iff P_{(G-p)/uv}(3) > 0. STRENGTH: an exact identity and an equivalent restatement of 17507; no lower bound. Landscape quantities (gap, ruggedness, entropy, OGP) bound only restricted algorithm classes (local or stable or low-degree), and zero-free regions give algorithms (Barvinok, Patel-Regts; from memory, verify); none quantifies over all algorithms.

Matches prediction for (a) and the sign part of (b). Not checked by this run: monotone decrease in (b), which the script did not report. statement: The edge-variable formula Phi(G) is exactly a perfect-matching encoding: its satisfying assignments correspond bijectively to perfect matchings of G. Thus the cubic-graph restriction translates positive 1-in-3 satisfiability into general-graph perfect matching, a polynomial-time problem; this is a structural reduction and makes no progress toward P != NP.

statement:
T50 (theory/T50-external-vpvnp-mechanism-and-boolean-transfer-2026-11-27.md): mechanism analysis of UNVERIFIED external VP!=VNP proofs (OpenAI Nov 23, Anthropic). Kept separate from established results; only the overviews have been read; Lean verification is pending. Owner decision recorded: T48 is consolidated, Q-BD is closed as a route, and the global contradiction mechanism is the focus.
Mechanism (both papers): a win-win dichotomy on a geometric hypothesis about tensor prices (spectral points/wire lengths). Flat case: rigidity, i.e. small rank across balanced cuts, gives a direct bound. Contracting case: wire saving lets a hypothetical small circuit be replayed faster, giving an accelerator (v^H steps in v^{H-16}) that iterates; a diagonal argument shows there are none (thm_noacc). The circuit enters only in two steps (arrows C: lem_balanced, lem_lowdeg), which use the block-multilinear and low-degree parts of the gate polynomials.
Boolean break point (B1): Boolean correctness lives in F[x]/I, which is only filtered, not graded (x^2 -> x). A Boolean circuit computes g = f + sum (x_i^2-x_i)h_i (Anthropic sec.2.5; = T49 Lemma3, T48 sec.3). The graded parts of g are not those of f; the explicit h_i (T48 8.1/9.1) do not help.
Required bridge MT (multilinearization transfer): a Boolean circuit of size s for multilinear f over F2 gives an arithmetic circuit of size poly(s) for f. NF(g) is always in VNP_2. (B2) MT plus the external theorem would only give parity-P not in P/poly (HC over F2 = parity of #HC; Valiant criterion, from memory), and P=NP is not known to imply parity-P in P/poly. Counting vs existence: no tool is known. (B3) The Boolean analogue of the accelerator diagonal needs a fixed exponent saving; P=NP gives only NTIME(t) in DTIME(t^c) with c>=1. The known Boolean speedup/slowdown contradictions are alternation trading (T27, closed).
First unproved implication on this route: MT. Together with the external theorem it is itself a Boolean lower bound, so it is not a small step, and it would still be parity-P, not NP. Next steps: Lean builds plus #print axioms, then the appendices (lem_balanced, lem_lowdeg, thm_noacc).

structure.conclusion: External VP!=VNP mechanism = geometric dichotomy (rigidity vs accelerator+diagonal); Boolean transfer breaks at grading (F[x]/I ungraded); bridge MT needed, would reach only parity-P; contracting-case Boolean analogue = closed T27

statement: Correction to my previous CONNECTION record (S-a711679438). The decision-to-search step (b) was argued by checking a search circuit's output against the table; that argument is not needed. Direction needed: a search-MCSP solver of size Õ(N) and depth Õ(1) has a flag output bit (1 iff some circuit of size <= s exists). That bit is a decision circuit with the same size and depth. So a lower bound 'no decision circuit of size N(log N)^k for any depth' implies 'search-MCSP[m^c] lacks Õ(N)-size, Õ(1)-depth circuits' for the fixed k. This is EXPLORATION-level reasoning, not a verified lemma. Still open: (a) whether MMW's 'lacks' means for all sufficiently large n or infinitely many n, (b) whether MMW's oracle A can be the empty oracle (A in PH is trivially allowed), (c) the exact search output convention in MMW. H1 remains a conditional hypothesis, not a known result; nothing here claims P != NP.

Source status: Fable's 'Addendum B' (padding lemma) and the owner's 'compatibility rank' are not in the PI files; their exact statements are not checked by the PI. Decision (owner): the structural growth parameter t is excluded as an independent proof route. Padding is recorded as negative knowledge. No return to the alternation route T27. U_G stays the primary object. PI-checkable part, t-copy padding of 17925: U_{G(t)}(X) = U_G evaluated at X_{v,c} = prod_{i<=t} X_{v,i,c}. For 3-colourable G it is homogeneous of degree t n (one variable per vertex copy); otherwise U_G = 0 and every padding is the zero polynomial. Circuit size grows at most additively by O(t n) multiplication gates for the substitution, so cost is not fully neutral. The growth is explained entirely by the explicit recoding, and the converse projection X_{v,i,c} = 1 for i >= 2 recovers U_G. Owner restriction, accepted: it is not proved that only time exponents and alternation depth are complexity-relevant parameters. Principle: treewidth, number of variables, polynomial degree and formal state space can all be changed by explicit recodings without changing the solution information (17921-17925). This explains why these structure measures do not capture general computational hardness. Semantic invariants (w_sem, and the compatibility rank per the owner) do not consume the hypothesis P = NP either. Next question (owner): which intrinsic properties of U_G would P = NP change or force? No obligation closed.

statement: DIRECTOR SYNTHESIS (classical facts (director's recollection of classical results; verify before citing)): the Tutte-barrier family on which the measured local GF(3) Nullstellensatz degree reached 4 (k=17) encodes PERFECT MATCHING, which is in P (Edmonds 1965). Edmonds' matching polytope = degree equations + odd-set inequalities, and odd-set inequalities are rank-1 Chvatal-Gomory cuts (sum the degree equations of an odd component, divide by 2, round). So cutting planes should refute these formulas with short proofs, exactly like the pigeonhole example: our NS-degree data on this family measure a LIMIT OF NULLSTELLENSATZ, not hardness of the problem. Test: short cutting-plane refutations of the k=5..17 instances.

statement: GRAPH-NATIVE TRANSFER OF THE CUT-FACTOR STEP FAILS FOR BOOLEAN COMPUTATION (PI 2026-11-27; CLAIMED, Claude family; standard fact). Graph: n disjoint 2-paths a_i-b_i-c_i; edge variables x_i={a_i,b_i}, y_i={b_i,c_i}. f(G) = parity of the number of i with both edges present (= inner product IP_n). Boolean circuit size O(n) (n AND + n-1 XOR). For the balanced edge cut {x} | {y}, the communication matrix has rank 2^n - 1 (0/1) and 2^n (+-1), checked numerically for n=2..8 (scratch ip_rank.py). Hence 'small computation on graph G implies low rank across balanced edge cuts' is false for Boolean gates. The OpenAI step exists_balanced_cutFactors needs homogeneous degree and parse grammar (sums of products), not graph structure. Consequence: a graph-native version of the geometric contradiction must either restrict to monotone/positive operations (then it is the arithmetic case of 17561, and Razborov's monotone bound for perfect matching, from memory, shows such bounds also hold for problems in P) or use a graph invariant that is NOT bounded by cut rank. No obligation closed.

statement: STATE-SUM INTEGRATION (owner 2026-11-27). SOURCE: 'Paths, trees and grids separate Valiant's hierarchy', OpenAI manuscript in the public repo openai/math, dated 2026-11-24, not peer-reviewed; per the repo's Lean doc the separations are Lean-checked for degree-component border circuits, and the explicit n^{Omega((log n)^{1/12})} grid bound is not formalised. Definition (paper eq. 1.1): Z_{G,q}(X) = sum_{a in [q]^E} prod_v X_{v, a|E(v)}, with an independent table at each vertex. IDENTITY (PI proof, statesum_check.py: path q=3, triangle, multi-edge, C4 equal as monomial multisets): Phi_{G,q} on positive exact-one clauses: per edge EO(y_{e,1..q}); per vertex EO(s_{v,alpha} : alpha in [q]^{E(v)}); for e in E(v), i in [q]: EO({y_{e,j}: j != i} u {s_{v,alpha}: alpha_e = i}), equivalent to y_{e,i} = sum_{alpha_e = i} s_{v,alpha}. The solutions are in bijection with a in [q]^E. Long clauses go to 3-ary positive exact-one parsimoniously: EO(x1,x2,z), EO(z,z',F), EO(z',x3,...), with z, z' determined and F the constant 0 from the T41 gadget E(T,a,b), E(T,b,c), E(T,c,a) (unique solution T=1, a=b=c=0). With weight X_{v,alpha} on s_{v,alpha} and 1 on every other variable, P_Phi(X) = sum_{y in Sol(Phi)} prod_{s_{v,alpha}=1} X_{v,alpha} = Z_{G,q}(X). So Z is a projection of the generic generating polynomial of an Exact-One family, and any arithmetic lower bound for Z transfers to it. ARITHMETIC vs BOOLEAN: the transfer stops at arithmetic circuits computing the polynomial formally. COUNTEREXAMPLE to any 'arithmetic generating-polynomial bound => Boolean decision bound' rule: bipartite perfect matching is decidable in P, yet its generating polynomial is the permanent (VNP-complete; the companion manuscript claims superpolynomial bounds for it). Known implications run the other way (Buergisser: NP not in P/poly plus GRH => VP != VNP over C, from memory, verify). No Boolean lower bound, no closure of OBL-R2/R6/R7/R8/ST-ABS/Q-C, and no P != NP progress follows, even if the manuscript is correct.

statement: INTERFERENCE = GF(3) CHARACTER SUMS (director synthesis for the spatiotemporal handover): a clause test x_i + x_j + x_k = 1 (mod 3) written with phases is (1/3) sum_t omega^{t(x_i+x_j+x_k-1)}, omega = e^{2 pi i/3}. Summed over the whole group F_3^n, the interference total is 3^(n-r) or 0 - exactly GF(3) consistency, computable by linear algebra, and blind to the 1,350 sets at n=6. Restricted to the Boolean cube {0,1}^n the same phases give the exact count Z(F) - a hypercube sum (VNP form), with no group structure to exploit. So a linear wave/interference model reproduces our known dichotomy: the efficient part is GF(3), the exact part is the hypercube sum. Readout: SAT formulas with exactly one solution exist (C = 1 rows in topic_onein3), so a normalised Boolean amplitude can be 2^-n. The QUBO energy E_F(x) = sum (x_i+x_j+x_k-1)^2 is an integer, so its SAT/UNSAT gap is always >= 1 (good readout margin) - the cost then sits in reaching the minimum, i.e. in the dynamics.

structure.question: Q-34b02a6004
structure.text: SOURCE CHECK row D (Stage A, lane T-B), verified at source. Chen-Jin-Santhanam-Williams, 'Constructive Separations and Their Consequences', arXiv 2203.14379, Theorem 1.7 (read verbatim from the web_read result at offset 22000, jina-reader extraction, paper p.9/41). Let s(n) >= n log(n)^{omega(1)} be time-constructive super-quasipolynomial; MCSP[s(n)] and Parity at input length N = 2^n. (1) If there exists a polylogtime-uniform AC0[quasipoly] refuter for MCSP[s(n)] against every polylogtime-uniform AC0 algorithm, then P != NP. (2) If PH not in SIZE(s(n)^2), there is a polylogtime-uniform AC0[quasipoly] refuter for MCSP[s(n)] against every polylogtime-uniform AC0 algorithm. (3) For s(n) <= o(2^n/n), there is a polylogtime-uniform AC0[2^poly(s(n))] refuter for MCSP[s(n)] against every polylogtime-uniform AC0 algorithm. (4) There is a polylogtime-uniform AC0[quasipoly] list-refuter for Parity against every polylogtime-uniform AC0 algorithm. statement: PRECISION to seq 17370 (owner 2026-11-27, checked against report sections 11/12; director). (1) REVIEW POINT CLOSED (owner): Lemma O only fixes selector variables and renames the rest; on the cube evaluation matrix this selects a submatrix, so rank cannot grow. Theorem 12 therefore holds for functional certificates 1 = sum_D a_D(x) Q_D(x) for all x in {0,1}^N with cube-rank widths; step (C) is not needed for the lower bound (it stays needed only to build a formal IPS identity). (2) Owner counterexample to reading 'linear' as individual degree 1: C = 1 - prod_j (1 - y_j) is multilinear, width <= 2, yet D_j = prod_{i<j}(1 - Q_i) and rank_{a|b} prod_{i<=k}(1 - a_i b_i) = 2^k (Kronecker product of rank-2 factors). Cost comes from multiplicative coupling between placeholders. Free extraction holds exactly for additively separable placeholders, C = A(x, y_{-j}) + y_j g_j(x) with g_j free of placeholders. Director note: 17370 defines N as placeholders occurring in a monomial with another placeholder or with degree >= 2; its complement is exactly the additively separable placeholders, so in the counterexample all y_j lie in N and the 17370 sharpening stands as written. Status unchanged: CLAIMED; novelty and independent review pending; full M9 open.

statement: CHROMATIC POLYNOMIAL (owner 2026-11-27; PI check). Whitney: P_G(q) = sum_{A subset E} (-1)^{|A|} q^{c(V,A)}. F(G) satisfiable iff P_G(3) > 0 (number of proper 3-colourings). Degree-2 membership (17507): e_p in W_G iff some colouring has col(u) = col(v); for uv not an edge, deletion-contraction gives P_{G+uv}(3) = P_G(3) - P_{G/uv}(3), and P_{G/uv}(3) counts exactly the colourings with col(u) = col(v); so e_p in W_G iff P_{G+uv}(3) < P_G(3) (if uv is an edge, both sides are false). Correct. KNOWN CANCELLATION THEORY: for the Tutte plane (P_G(q) is a Tutte evaluation at (1-q, 0)), Jaeger-Vertigan-Welsh 1990 (from memory, verify) prove #P-hardness except on the hyperbola (x-1)(y-1) = 1 and a few special points, where the Whitney sum collapses (e.g. matrix-tree, a determinant). q = 3 gives (-2, 0), (x-1)(y-1) = 3, hard. So exponential term count is not cost, and the efficient cancellations of this family are classified, but only relative to #P-hardness. An unconditional cancellation-impossibility theorem for P_G(3) is a Boolean lower bound (P_G(3) as a function of the graph's bits), and the multivariate Potts generating polynomial in edge weights is the arithmetic object of 17540, where arithmetic hardness does not transfer.

structure.text: SOURCE CHECK (Chen-Jin-Williams, 'Hardness Magnification for all Sparse NP Languages', FOCS 2019 PDF, extracted text at offsets 9000-13500; ECCC numbering may differ). (1) Theorem I.1 hypothesis quantifies over all beta in (0,1), not only small beta. (2) Theorem I.6 item 1: if search-MCSP[s(m)] is not in Circuit[n*poly(s(m))], with n=2^m and m <= s(m) <= 2^{(1-Omega(1))m}, then NP is not in Circuit[poly(n)]. Item 1 has no beta-range restriction and covers s(m)=m^c for c>=1. The 'for all small enough beta>0' wording appears in item 7 (TC^d with search-MCSP[2^{beta m}]) and in the prior-work paragraph on Oliveira-Santhanam, not in item 1. (3) So the beta-near-1 concern from S0022 does not apply to the K10 Stage C route with s=m^c; the admissible-beta lemma (Q-8eca0d9fa6, S0022) is needed only for item 7. (4) Open: item 1 needs a lower bound for search-MCSP[m^c] outside Circuit[2^m * m^{O(c)}], which is exactly the open K10 obligation. No progress toward P != NP from this check. Barrier note: no LOWER_BOUND is recorded here; this is a source check only.

statement: RECURSIVE COMPOSITION + MinGraph CANNOT YIELD A CONTRADICTION (PI 2026-11-27; CLAIMED, Claude family). Owner transfer: R_{j+1}(a,b) <-> exists c R_j(a,c) & R_j(c,b), G_{j+1} = MinGraph(G_j o G_j); under P=NP the run time is poly(s, K_max, log T). Correct as stated. (1) Strength of the premise: K_max = poly(s) for all transition maps with s-bit state means every DSPACE(s) computation has a poly(s)-size EXISTENTIAL graph representation, i.e. PSPACE inside NP/poly. Unproven and believed false. With only exists-quantifiers the size doubles per level; the Savitch/TQBF reuse of one copy needs a forall per level, i.e. log T = poly alternations, outside every fixed level of PH, so P=NP does not collapse it. (2) Even with the premise the conclusion is P=PSPACE: DTIME(t) in DSPACE(t) in DTIME(t^d) contradicts no hierarchy theorem. Relative to A = TQBF we have P^A = NP^A = PSPACE^A, and all steps relativize, so no contradiction is possible. EXP would need exponential state s, so K_max >= s is exponential. (3) The affine case M^{2^k} by repeated squaring is correct but trivial (the affine class is closed under composition). No obligation closed.

statement: T41-D6 JOINT SCHUR (owner 2026-11-27), CLAIMED, author-checked (Claude family): schur_t41_check.py, 400 random read<=3 positive 1-in-3 instances, 2644 principal minors, parity over F_2 and weighted over GF(2^19). (a) W subset V\T maximal nonsingular principal block of B[V\T] (principal rank property, symmetric): det B[V\U] = det C * det K[Wbar\U] for all U subset T; K[R,R]=0 with |R| = nu = dim ker B[V\T]; nu > |T\U| kills the term; nu > |T| => #SAT even. (b) Weighted B(X) (one weight per 1-2-occurrence variable, char 2): det B(X)[V\U(S)] != 0 <=> residual instance satisfiable (cycles >=3 cancel in reverse pairs, covers give distinct monomials); nu(X) > |T| => unsatisfiable; kernel |T|+nu <= 2|T|; randomized poly preprocessing over GF(2^{|H|+O(log m)}). Strength: (a) is the principal pivot transform; nu > |T| is a deficiency/pigeonhole certificate (each uncoverable clause of V\T needs its own T clause), never triggered in the sample; cost of the remaining sum unchanged, poly*2^|H|, and |T| = Theta(m) in the R3 hard regime. (c) Delta-matroid placement, checked at the source (Eiben-Koana-Wahlstroem arXiv 2502.13654 / ESA 2026, Sec. 1.2): satisfiable <=> some U exactly a disjoint union of E_h is feasible in D(B) twisted by V. Theorem 6 (FPT k^O(k)) is Triangle Cover with F subset V(T') (partial triangles allowed); the exactly-partitioned variant is 3-Delta-matroid Parity, stated W[1]-hard there. Their linear delta-matroids are skew-symmetric with zero diagonal in char 2; our B has a diagonal (private variables). So the reduction lands on the W[1]-hard side; no algorithm follows. No obligation closed.

statement: SOURCE CHECK, MMW19 Thm 1.2 and Thm 1.3, verbatim from the primary PDF (sha256 7077714b...), read this session. Thm 1.2: for time-constructible s(n) >= n and any oracle A, a one-pass streaming algorithm for search-MCSP^A[s(n)] on 2^n-bit inputs runs in 2^n * Otilde(s(n)) time, with Otilde(s(n)^2) update time and Otilde(s(n)) space, using a Sigma3SAT^A oracle with queries of length Otilde(s(n)). Thm 1.3: if some time-constructible s(n) >= n and A in PH make search-MCSP^A[s(n)] unsolvable by a poly(s(n))-space streaming algorithm with poly(s(n)) update time, then P != NP. Proof idea (Thm 1.3): P=NP makes the Sigma3SAT^A oracle calls of Thm 1.2 polynomial, so the hypothesis of Thm 1.3 would fail. The authors note streaming algorithms need not read a fresh bit each step. Not yet read: the Section 5 proof and whether the update-time bound is worst-case. Consequence for Q-eed0582acc: Thm 1.2/1.3 concern a one-pass streaming model with a Sigma3SAT oracle and polynomial-update-time lower bounds, not the randomized streaming model with DISJ or AC0 of CJSW Thm 1.3-1.7. Whether K1 falls under Thm 1.3 is still open until CJSW Thm 1.3 f(n) is read.

statement: RELATIONAL FACTORISATION - logical strength (director, 2026-11-26; no new lane, under CONV-D seq 17216). By the owner's constant-block counterexample (tool map row), for q = N^{beta+o(1)} blocks all local predicates can be trivial while the inter-block relation carries the whole Gap-MCSP hardness: on x(j,z) = g(j) the relation IS Gap-MCSP of the q-bit table g. A request for an 'efficient formula for the cross-block consistency relation of MCSP' is therefore a reformulation of the target, not a reduction. It becomes a genuine sub-obligation only together with a PROVEN structure of that relation (equality-type, low rank, bounded interface) that makes it cheaper than Gap-MCSP itself; none is known, and FOURIER-SUP seq 17183 and TRUNC2 seq 17202 (lossless, full-rank interfaces) point against a low-rank structure. The open point is thus: a non-product, non-enumerative formula for the shared-witness coupling (SEP-MERGE-LB excludes product forms, SEP-ELIM-LB excludes separator analyses independent of the hypothesis circuits).

statement: CONTROL THEOREM K AND STATUS AFTER THE OWNER CHECK OF THEOREM H (CLAIMED; cross-family mission iteration 14 submitted). (1) Owner algebraic check of Theorem H step 4 (17916): agrees with the PI exact kernel computation. Gadget rows give C_0 = C_1 = C_2; the triangle gives A + B + C = 0, hence A_0 = A_1 = A_2; line sums give multiples of J. Steps 5 and 6 give divisibility inside L_G, not only coordinatewise. No assumption on G beyond unpinned and 3-colourable. (2) Theorem K (owner): let S be a nonempty affine subspace of F3^n of codimension r. Then acn(F3^n minus S) = 2r. Proof checked by PI. Translate and quotient by the direction space of S to reach F3^r minus {0}. The cover x_i = 1, x_i = 2 gives <= 2r. For the lower bound, every covering subspace avoids 0, so it lies in an affine hyperplane l_i = 1 with l_i linear (choose l_i zero on the direction space and 1 at a base point). Then P = prod (1 - l_i) is the indicator of 0. Its reduced form is prod_j (1 - x_j^2) of degree 2r, and reduction does not raise degree, so k >= 2r. Literature: the hyperplane case is Alon-Fueredi 1993 (covering all but one point of a grid needs sum(|S_i| - 1) hyperplanes; here 2r). The extension from subspaces to hyperplanes is immediate. Related: Jamison 1977, Brouwer-Schrijver 1978 (blocking sets, k(q-1)+1). Alon-Fueredi and Brouwer-Schrijver were seen via search results; the Jamison citation is not verified at the source. K is therefore classical, not new. (3) Use: an exact per-stage optimum for the Gauss control. At stage t (eliminated set E) the projection of S = {Ax = b} has codimension rank A - rank A_E, so the optimum is 2(rank A - rank A_E), or 1 if S is empty. (4) Owner restriction of Fable's conclusion, accepted. 'Prism gives no extra simplification' is proved for the full pinned colouring set. For the positive representation, every projection creates only per-component shifts of G[T] (17915 R3). For the complement representation and arbitrary elimination orders it is not proved. The identification of existence elimination with dag-like resolution over linear equations mod 3 needs a formal simulation (F3-valued vs 0/1 variables); not done. (5) Status: prism lattice theorem algebraically checked by PI and owner; U_H with gadget variables is an exact identity; merging calculus is incomplete (17917); K is exact and classical. A proof of P != NP remains open. No obligation closed.

statement: OWNER DEEP RESEARCH 2026-11-19 (interface entropy -> P vs NP) with director source check: (a) no universal transfer from treewidth/separators/NOF to arbitrary algorithms; NOF -> ACC0 only (Hastad-Goldmann, Beigel-Tarui); P not in ACC0 does not give P != NC1. (b) Owner counterexample (exact): D_r = AND_{i<j} EXACT1(a,y_i,y_j) has treewidth r and is SAT (a=1, y=0); glued to F8 via a (GF(3) solution shifted so a=1, y=0) it is GF(3)-consistent, UNSAT, connected, of unbounded treewidth, with a constant-size core - large treewidth of a formula does not imply hardness (the family is refuted in poly time by bounded-width resolution). (c) Sources checked by the director on the web: ETH refutation claims by OpenAI and Anthropic (late Oct 2026, ~2^{n/(log n)^{1/2+o(1)}} for fixed-width k-SAT/#SAT) are widely reported (TechCrunch 2026-10-27, Fortnow blog) but independent verification is still in progress; Lean is reported for OpenAI, for Anthropic unconfirmed. Chukhin-Gajulapalli-Golovnev-Mihajlin (arXiv 2611.07972, ECCC TR26-313) confirmed: unconditional NE not in SIZE(2^n/(2n)) OR VP0_Z != VNP0_Z. Mishra-Santhanam 4n-O(log n) general-circuit bound: found only as a STOC 2027 submission claim (depends on Li s affine dispersers) - unverified. (d) Evaluation rule: algorithmic results also count through proved algorithm-to-lower-bound transfers (Williams; PIT), added to the research brief; a 2^{o(n)} k-SAT algorithm alone is no P-time algorithm and does not by itself give a new circuit lower bound (CNF lower bounds are already known).

statement: LEMMA W - status corrected (owner review 2026-11-19): it is the EASY direction of Hlineny-Whittle, 'Matroid tree-width', Theorem 3.2 (tree-width of a graph G with an edge equals the tree-width of its cycle matroid M(G)), restated for represented matroids: rows with supports as cliques of the coefficient graph instead of edges as cliques of G. Definition checked against the paper (final version, fi.muni.cz/~hlineny/papers/matr-tw-final.pdf, eq. (MW)): node width = sum_i r_M(E - F_i) - (d-1) r(M), exactly as used. The argument (map each element to a bag containing its support; ranks of the branch complements bounded by bag size) is the standard one; treat it as a straightforward / folklore generalisation, NOT as a new or 'proposed' result. The +1 (rank of a bag's coordinate vectors is <= |bag|, vs |bag| - 1 for a spanning forest of a graphic bag) is the only difference to the graphic case. A source stating the matrix version explicitly was not found in a short search (Cunningham-Geelen IPCO 2007 / ILP branch-width literature is the likely place).

statement: Dispute K11-D5, verified source step. MMW19 (STOC 2019) Thm 1.4, third bullet, read from the primary PDF (people.csail.mit.edu/rrw/MCSP-MKTP-stoc19.pdf, offset 13500, sha256 7077714b...): for s(n) >= n and A in PH, if search-MCSP^A[s(n)] on inputs of length N=2^n does not have circuits of N*poly(s(n)) size and poly(s(n)) depth, then NP not in P/poly. CONSEQUENCES: (a) with A = empty oracle (in PH) and s(n)=n^c, a lower bound for DECISION MCSP[m^c] against general circuits of size N*(log N)^k (any depth) gives the search hypothesis, because a search solver's flag bit is a decision circuit of the same size and depth; (b) therefore no separate H2 premise is needed, and NP-in-P/poly-to-small-MCSP-circuits is carried by the theorem. OPEN: (i) the quantifier in Thm 1.4 ('for all n' vs 'infinitely many n') is not yet read; (ii) H1 itself, a general-circuit lower bound N*polylog(N) for decision MCSP[m^c], is unproved and is the real remaining obligation (see Q-f1e058b72f). The transfer relativizes (any oracle in PH). This is a magnification connection, not a LOWER_BOUND record.

statement: UNIT-VECTOR NEGATIVE TEST (owner 2026-11-26, director checked; documentation, GRID-DEG stays closed). R_G(X) = prod_{e={u,v}} sum_c M_{u,e,c} M_{v,e,c} with M_{v,e,c} = sum_{alpha: alpha(e)=c} X_{v,alpha}: on X_v = e_{j_v} the factor is [alpha_u(e) = alpha_v(e)], so R_G = H = Z on all unit-vector inputs; arithmetic circuit size O(d q^4) (d*deg*q sums of q^3 variables plus e*q products), deg R_G = 2e. Consistent with the GRID-DEG bound: deg excess k = 2e - d ~ 3d gives (S+1) 2^{O(d)} q^{O(d)}, no contradiction. statement: P != NP TRACK FILTERS (2026-11-20, spec section "P != NP track - mandatory filters"): F1 sparsity cap - a language with <= S yes-instances per length has cut matrices with <= S ones, rank <= S and read-once width <= S+1 in every order; for MCSP[s] log S = O~(s), so no cut/rank/restriction measure can prove the MMW19 streaming target. F2 locality - with a PH oracle the streaming algorithm exists (MMW19 Thm 1.2); arguments surviving oracle gates on poly(s) bits are dead. Target in our model: no read-once program with poly(s) state bits and poly(s)-time transition function for MCSP^A[s]; needs a measure on transition functions; OPEN, no candidate.

statement: Separation of verified fact vs novelty for T9. VERIFIED FACTS (four-way exact, keep): (1) Sigma(perm_5) has a genuine smooth 11-dim component V_{2,3} through X_A (dim T_{X_A}Sigma=11 forces the component through X_A to be dim 11; the 15-dim pieces of the enclosing partition variety carry a zero row, which X_A lacks); (2) Sigma(perm_5) is NOT equidimensional (dim 11 and 15 components). NOT ESTABLISHED: that this is the FIRST proof of non-equidimensionality (prior art unresolved); that it refutes Conjecture 4.27 (it does not - V_{2,3} is in a predicted partition variety). A genuine attack on Conj 4.27 would need a singular point lying in NO partition variety; we do NOT have one. Dimension note (corrected): the partition product variety has global dim dim P_{2,5}+dim P_{3,5}=5+10=15 (Xie Thm), but that does not exclude its own dim-11 sub-component V_{2,3} (Thm 3.18/1.1 claim no equidimensionality).

statement: FULL READ of Hlinený–Whittle matr-tw-final.pdf (sha256 0cd3e9f9..., chars 0-33860). Main Thm 3.2: tw(G) = tw(P) = tw(M(G)) for simple graphs, via point-configuration tree-width (Lemmas 5.1, 5.2, 5.4; Claims 5.3, 5.5, 5.6). Lemma 5.1 gives only one direction for graphs (tw(P) <= tw(G)); the converse is Lemma 5.4. The paper defines tree-width of a matroid or point configuration only; it does NOT state any minimum over kernel bases of a coefficient graph H_B, nor any blow-up construction, nor the identity w*(F(G)) = 2tw(G)+1. Conclusion: the paper is the nearest published context (matroid tw = graph tw) but does not cover the minimum-over-bases statement. statement: WITNESS GENERATOR from D-018 (owner 2026-11-19): adding a constant c to all coordinates keeps every clause sum mod 3 (3c = 0), and two distinct values can always be shifted onto {0,1}; a constant vector is never a solution. Hence every GF(3) solution of a BLIND formula uses all three values, and every blind formula on n variables is, up to isomorphism, a subset of the clauses allowed by a witness with value counts (k0,k1,k2), all >= 1, up to cyclic shift. n=7: 5 types, 2^10+2^10+2^12+2^13+2^11 = 16,384 candidate clause sets instead of 2^35. Upper bounds on candidates: n=6: 320, n=7: 16,384, n=8: 5,046,272, n=9: 12,519,997,440 (before dedup). Minimal-UNSAT reduction: every UNSAT formula contains an MUS; a GF(3)-inconsistent MUS has no integer solution and is refuted by one CG round (D-023); adding clauses only shrinks the first CG closure - so the maximal CG rank over all UNSAT formulas on <= n variables is attained on blind MUS classes.

Upper bounds on candidates: n=6: 320, n=7: 16,384, n=8: 5,046,272, n=9: 12,519,997,440 (before dedup). Minimal-UNSAT reduction: every UNSAT formula contains an MUS; a GF(3)-inconsistent MUS has no integer solution and is refuted by one CG round (D-023); adding clauses only shrinks the first CG closure - so the maximal CG rank over all UNSAT formulas on <= n variables is attained on blind MUS classes.

statement: STAGE A SOURCE CHECK, row B, closed against the primary PDF (people.csail.mit.edu/rrw/MCSP-MKTP-stoc19.pdf, sha256 7077714b...). Thm 1.4 (verbatim): for s(n) >= n and A in PH, if there is eps>0 such that for all c>=1, search-MCSP^A[2^{eps n/c}] on inputs of length N=2^n has no N^{1+eps}-size O(1/eps)-depth TC0 circuits, then NP is not in TC0. The same paper's Thm 1.3 hypothesis is a super-linear-time worst-case lower bound for search-MCSP against deterministic streaming algorithms with sub-linear space. Row B's earlier citation (a circuit-to-formula route via Thm 1.4) is WRONG: Thm 1.4 is a TC0 result for the search version with an oracle A in PH. The text also confirms that OPS18 uses an O(n)-approximation MCSP[2^{eps n}] with N^{1+delta}-size circuits to get NP not in P/poly, consistent with row A.

statement: PI CHECK OF THE 2026-11-27 OWNER SYNTHESIS (elimination identities, lattices, Kempe, prism; CLAIMED, Claude family; Fable's review is also Claude family, so no cross-family review yet). (1) Elimination identities: correct. Q(t,u) = R(u) prod_{j<=d} (t - r_j(u))^2. For d <= 2, exists t with Q = 1 iff R = 1. For d = 3, three elements of F3 are pairwise distinct iff r1+r2+r3 = 0 and r1 != r2. If r1+r2+r3 = 0 and r1 != r2, then r3 = r1 would give r2 = -2r1 = r1. These are the 3-factor case of the closure lemma 17910: the bad set {sum = 0, r1 - r2 = 1} union {sum = 0, r1 - r2 = 2} consists of two codim-2 subspaces instead of six codim-3 points. (2) Union rule: U cup (v+U) cup (2v+U) = U + <v> over F3. Implemented as coset merging {Ax in b + <d>} = {CAx = Cb} with ker C = <d>, to a fixpoint, then pruning (scratchpad/aelim/merge.py). 0/150 mismatches against brute force. Peaks on random 3-colouring at m = 2.3n, n = 8..16, 3 seeds: 17-47 subspaces with merging against 27-115 without, about 2.2-2.9n. Small sizes only; no asymptotic claim. (3) Satz A, arbitrary order (owner strengthening): proof correct. Project to r coordinates injective on the Q-span; generators have entries in {-1,0,1}, so norm <= sqrt r. A rank step multiplies the covolume by at most sqrt r, a same-rank strict extension divides it by at least 2, and the final covolume is >= 1. So k <= (r/2) log2 r, and Fable's two-phase restriction is unnecessary. (4) Satz B, 3L <= M <= L: correct for unpinned graphs only. Fable's pinned counterexample is accepted: pinned prism, ranks 3 and 2 over Q. (5) Lemma F, general form: correct. If S is closed under global colour permutations, x + rho x + rho^2 x = 1 and q is invariant, then an affine q = Bx + b is constant on S in char != 3. (6) Universal prism transformation H(G), |V| = 7n+3, a_v = bottom vertex opposite R0 of prism A_v, b_v = bottom vertex opposite R1 of prism B_v, triangle v a_v b_v. (a) Each colour of v has exactly one extension (table checked by hand), so Col3(H) = 6 |Col3(G)|. (b) PI proof that each colour pair {c,c'} induces a connected subgraph in every colouring. A prism bottom vertex p_i of colour c is adjacent to R_{c'} if i = c'. Otherwise i is the third colour, and its bottom neighbour of colour c' sits at index c, hence is adjacent to R_c. Every original v of colour c has a neighbour in {a_v, b_v} of colour c'. So Kempe swaps are global transpositions and #Kempe classes = |Col3(G)|. (c) [L_H : M_H] = 3^r with r = rank_Q of the one-hot colouring differences of G: verified exactly (integer HNF) on 15 graphs, among them K3, C5, C6 and G = prism, where rank_F3 = 7 < rank_Q = 8 and the index is still 3^8. Upper bound proved: L/M is generated by the image of W ~ L_G (rank r) and killed by 3. Lower bound open: the prism readouts epsilon give only 3^{rank_F3}, which is insufficient for G = prism. The owner's tensor argument L/M ~ W (x) (T/J) has unproved steps (injectivity, the separate summand). So (c) is computational evidence plus a proved upper bound, not a theorem. (7) Relevance: the index is 3^{2n} already for edgeless G, so it carries no hardness. (8) First unproved statement of the strongest chain (Phase 3 of the owner plan): a property that polynomial-time selection S must have and that contradicts a proved theorem. None has been derived. Every consequence derived so far (selection, lattice generators, tropical value, elimination) relativizes (cf. 17590) or also holds for exponential-time algorithms. No obligation closed.

If S is closed under global colour permutations, x + rho x + rho^2 x = 1 and q is invariant, then an affine q = Bx + b is constant on S in char != 3. (6) Universal prism transformation H(G), |V| = 7n+3, a_v = bottom vertex opposite R0 of prism A_v, b_v = bottom vertex opposite R1 of prism B_v, triangle v a_v b_v. (a) Each colour of v has exactly one extension (table checked by hand), so Col3(H) = 6 |Col3(G)|. (b) PI proof that each colour pair {c,c'} induces a connected subgraph in every colouring. A prism bottom vertex p_i of colour c is adjacent to R_{c'} if i = c'. Otherwise i is the third colour, and its bottom neighbour of colour c' sits at index c, hence is adjacent to R_c. Every original v of colour c has a neighbour in {a_v, b_v} of colour c'. So Kempe swaps are global transpositions and #Kempe classes = |Col3(G)|. (c) [L_H : M_H] = 3^r with r = rank_Q of the one-hot colouring differences of G: verified exactly (integer HNF) on 15 graphs, among them K3, C5, C6 and G = prism, where rank_F3 = 7 < rank_Q = 8 and the index is still 3^8. Upper bound proved: L/M is generated by the image of W ~ L_G (rank r) and killed by 3. Lower bound open: the prism readouts epsilon give only 3^{rank_F3}, which is insufficient for G = prism. The owner's tensor argument L/M ~ W (x) (T/J) has unproved steps (injectivity, the separate summand). So (c) is computational evidence plus a proved upper bound, not a theorem. (7) Relevance: the index is 3^{2n} already for edgeless G, so it carries no hardness. (8) First unproved statement of the strongest chain (Phase 3 of the owner plan): a property that polynomial-time selection S must have and that contradicts a proved theorem. None has been derived. Every consequence derived so far (selection, lattice generators, tropical value, elimination) relativizes (cf. 17590) or also holds for exponential-time algorithms. No obligation closed.
